original_question: Determine whether the incompressible Euler equations are ill-posed in the Besov spaces B^1_{infinity,q} for 1 < q < infinity.
target_in_paper: §5.1, Problem 7: “Are the Euler equations (1.1) ill-posed in the Besov spaces B^1_{∞,q} for 1 < q < ∞?” ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct PDE, the exact Besov scale B^1_{∞,q}, and the precise range 1 < q < ∞; it is essentially the wording of Problem 7 itself. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
missing_details: The paper poses this as a question about the local Cauchy problem, so “ill-posed” should be understood locally rather than as an unspecified global failure. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

Section 5.1 defines ill-posedness in the Hadamard Banach-space sense: local existence, uniqueness, and continuous dependence in C([0,T],X); the refined question should make that sense explicit. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, the Euler system should be written explicitly as ∂_t v + v·∇v = -∇p, div v = 0, with initial condition v(0)=v_0. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The ambient spatial setting from §1 is a fixed fluid domain M, with the velocity field tangent to ∂M when the boundary is nonempty; this is implicit in the draft but explicit in the paper’s formulation of (1.1). ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))

The nearby context explains that this is the remaining intermediate Besov range between known refined well-posedness results in B^1_{∞,1} and known ill-posedness/loss-of-regularity phenomena in B^1_{∞,∞}, F^1_{∞,2}, and log Lip^α; that positioning is implicit in the draft. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
The quantifier is over the full family of indices 1 < q < ∞, not just a single unspecified q. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
refined_question: For the local Cauchy problem for the incompressible Euler equations ∂_t v + v·∇v = -∇p, div v = 0, v(0)=v_0, on a fixed fluid domain M, with v tangent to ∂M when ∂M ≠ ∅, is the problem ill-posed in the Hadamard sense in the Besov spaces B^1_{∞,q}(M) for every intermediate index 1 < q < ∞? ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
justification: This is the nearest official target because §5.1 is specifically devoted to local well-posedness of the Cauchy problem, and Problem 7 asks almost exactly what your draft asks. The only needed sharpening is to restore the paper’s implicit analytic setup: the precise Euler system from (1.1), the boundary convention on M, and the Hadamard meaning of “ill-posed.” The paragraph surrounding Problem 7 also shows that the authors are isolating the unresolved intermediate Besov scale between the endpoint spaces B^1_{∞,1} and B^1_{∞,∞}. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD2205.01143.pdf))
